newsitem.title: UK: Huge hole in Labour plans, says UK's Heseltine.
newsitem.headline: Huge hole in Labour plans, says UK's Heseltine.

text.p: British deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine said on Thursday there was a 1.5 billion pounds ($2.5 billion) hole in the opposition Labour party's budget, unveiled earlier in the day.
Heseltine told a news conference there was a "black hole" because Labour had pledged to follow the ruling Conservative party's budget plans if it won a May 1 election.

But he said the overall budget prepared by the government for the 1998-1999 fiscal year included 1.5 billion pounds in revenue from privatisation receipts, while the Labour party had not announced any privatisation plans.
"It is absolutely clear that Labour would have to privatise to cover the black hole or else raise taxes," Heseltine said.

Heseltine said the Conservatives had not specified which privatisations they would carry out to bring in the 1.5 billion, although these could include selling the national air traffic services or Royal Mail subsidiaries, such as Parcelforce.
But Heseltine said the unions and Labour's left wing would prevent the opposition's economic spokesman Gordon Brown pushing through privatisations to fill this budget hole.
Brown told a BBC radio interviewer that he had not ruled out privatising the air traffic control system.
But he said a judgement had to be made whether revenue lost in a privatisation was outweighed by the capital return.
